title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Further Strengthening the Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property Rights
keywords_en: copyright; patent right; trademark right; guarantee; administrative litigation; administrative penalty; copyright infringement; intellectual property
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Further Strengthening Judicial Protection of Intellectual Property

Fa [1994] No. 111

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army:

Strict enforcement of the law and protection of intellectual property rights in accordance with the law are of great significance for promoting the prosperity and development of science, technology, and cultural undertakings, and for ensuring the normal operation of the socialist market economy. In recent years, people's courts at all levels have implemented and enforced laws and regulations on the protection of intellectual property rights, heard intellectual property cases correctly and promptly, protected the lawful rights and interests of the parties, and promoted the development and prosperity of socialist culture and science. In order to further strengthen the judicial protection of intellectual property and ensure the implementation of the laws, the following notice is hereby given:

1. Further strengthen the adjudication force and improve the adjudication organs. Intellectual property litigation is highly professional and technical, and there are many foreign-related cases. People's courts undertaking the trial of intellectual property cases should select and assign an appropriate number of adjudicators with certain trial experience, paying special attention to selecting personnel who have studied science and engineering and have knowledge of foreign languages to participate in intellectual property adjudication work. They should also form collegial panels specifically for hearing intellectual property cases as needed. Intermediate people's courts and high people's courts in large and medium-sized cities with a high volume of intellectual property cases may, if conditions permit, establish intellectual property adjudication divisions to concentrate on hearing intellectual property cases, thereby ensuring timely and fair handling of such cases.

2. In accordance with the provisions of laws and relevant judicial interpretations, people's courts at all levels shall promptly accept various civil and administrative cases involving infringement of intellectual property rights that meet the conditions for prosecution. Disputes over copyright infringement shall be accepted by the civil adjudication division (if an intellectual property adjudication division is established, it shall be accepted by that division). Disputes over trademark and patent infringement shall be accepted by the economic adjudication division (if an intellectual property adjudication division is established, it shall be accepted by that division). Disputes over liability for compensation and the amount of compensation in intellectual property cases, after mediation by the competent administrative department, where a party is dissatisfied and brings a civil lawsuit to the people's court, shall be accepted by the civil adjudication division or the economic adjudication division (if an intellectual property adjudication division is established, it shall be accepted by that division). Where a party is dissatisfied with an administrative penalty decision made by an administrative department for intellectual property and brings an administrative lawsuit to the people's court, it shall be accepted by the administrative adjudication division. Currently, the number of civil and administrative cases of intellectual property infringement is increasing substantially. People's courts at all levels must resolutely resist local protectionism and departmental protectionism, strictly implement laws and regulations on the protection of intellectual property, and protect the lawful rights and interests of the parties in accordance with the law.

When hearing intellectual property cases, people's courts shall strictly apply the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China, the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, the Technology Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China, and the Anti-Unfair Competition Law of the People's Republic of China, as well as other laws and regulations and international treaties concerning intellectual property that China has acceded to or concluded. They shall fully, equally, and promptly protect the lawful rights and interests of the parties, and severely sanction various illegal acts of infringing intellectual property rights. For civil infringements, in addition to ordering the infringer to bear civil liabilities such as cessation of infringement, elimination of adverse effects, making an apology, and compensating for losses, the court may also, depending on the specific circumstances of the case, impose sanctions such as confiscation of illegal gains, fines, or detention on the actor in accordance with the law.

3. Intensify the crackdown and severely punish various criminal acts of infringing intellectual property rights. The Decision on Punishing Crimes of Copyright Infringement (hereinafter referred to as the Decision) deliberated and adopted by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress is a powerful legal weapon for punishing crimes of copyright infringement. People's courts at all levels shall seriously implement it. For cases that violate the Decision and constitute a crime, where the victim directly files a lawsuit with the people's court, the people's court may accept the case directly, except for those that seriously endanger social order or national interests.

Pursuant to the Supplementary Provisions of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Punishing Crimes of Counterfeiting Registered Trademarks and the relevant provisions of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, for acts of counterfeiting registered trademarks and counterfeiting another person's patent that constitute a crime, the criminal liability of the persons concerned shall be investigated in accordance with the law. For theft of important technological achievements, criminal liability shall be investigated in accordance with the law under the crime of theft.

4. Strengthen the training of professional and technical knowledge and legal knowledge for intellectual property adjudicators, and strive to improve the level of law enforcement. People's courts in all localities shall, through study classes, training courses, seminars, symposiums, and other forms, organize relevant adjudicators, in connection with the actual work of adjudication, to seriously study and research the science and technology related to intellectual property, laws and regulations on the protection of intellectual property, and international treaties concerning intellectual property that China has acceded to or concluded. They should also pay attention to summarizing the trial experience of intellectual property cases through adjudication practice, thereby improving the level of judicial protection of intellectual property.

5. High people's courts at all levels shall strengthen supervision and guidance over the lower people's courts in hearing intellectual property cases. Through investigation and research, they shall continuously summarize the experience of hearing intellectual property cases, improve the quality of case handling. At the same time, they shall establish a reporting system for major and important cases, strengthen the inspection of intellectual property cases heard within their jurisdiction, focusing on inspecting major and influential intellectual property infringement cases, and urge the correction of lax law enforcement practices that exist in some localities, so as to effectively ensure the implementation of intellectual property laws and regulations.

6. Combine case handling with strengthening publicity and education work. In particular, people's courts in areas with a high incidence of intellectual property infringement cases shall, based on local specific conditions, select some typical cases, and through public sentencing and various forms such as news media, publicize laws and regulations on intellectual property, popularize legal knowledge on the protection of intellectual property, and enhance the awareness of intellectual property protection and the concept of legality in the whole society.

September 29, 1994
